episodes.169253: A cluster of strong thunderstorms over northwestern Crook County produced hail and gusty winds.
episodes.169303: A line of showers and thunderstorms associated with an area of low pressure in the western Gulf of Mexico produced a gust of 35 knots at Buoy 42020 the morning of June 29th.
episodes.169330: Scattered slow moving thunderstorms formed in a moist environment.  Locally heavy rain fell in Richland Co SC, around 3 to 4 inches, in the morning to midday hours and produced some flooding.
episodes.169343: A cold front ahead of a Pacific trough moving through southern Canada set off a round of strong to severe thunderstorms during the evening hours.
episodes.169384: An isolated downburst caused brief severe wind conditions at Tonopah Airport.
episodes.169456: Monsoon moisture plus a weak trough approaching from the west fueled scattered thunderstorms over Mohave County. Some storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.169468: Gusty winds accompanied a cluster of thunderstorms over southern Butte County. Wind gusts near 60 mph were reported in the Belle Fourche area.
episodes.169469: A thunderstorm intensified over portions of Haakon County, producing wind gusts as high as 90 mph in a few areas.
episodes.169471: A thunderstorm became severe as it tracked over Jackson County. Wind gusts over 60 mph were reported.
episodes.169473: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked east-northeast from far northeastern Wyoming and southeastern Montana across northwest South Dakota. The storms produced wind gusts near 70 mph.
episodes.169477: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across south central South Dakota, producing wind gusts over 70 mph.
episodes.169553: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.169694: A cluster of thunderstorms brought wind damage to the Mission Valley during the evening hours of June 28.
episodes.169914: An isolated severe wind gust occurred just southeast of Big Horn.
episodes.169915: An isolated severe wind gust occurred in Ridge.
episodes.170201: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front. Some of these storms produced large hail and strong wind gusts.
episodes.170236: Two clusters of eastward-moving strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the evening of the 29th. The first was associated with weak low pressure across south central South Dakota, and the second was triggered by a cold front across north central South Dakota, both in hot environments with daytime highs in the 90s. These storms produced 60 to 70 mph or greater wind gusts, including 68 mph six miles southwest of the Joe Creek Rec Area, and damaged trees and other property across the area. High non-thunderstorm winds developed across east central South Dakota during the evening as well, the highest measured being 63 mph four miles west of Bryant.
episodes.170289: A trough hot on the heels of an upper ridge resulted in moist southwesterly flow across the region. Approaching trough created a weak surface low in the vicinity, which resulted in better surface moisture being advected in from the east. A front provided a source of lift for thunderstorms on this day.
episodes.170312: Light southeast steering flow prevailed across the area with a prevailing east coast sea breeze regime with an inverted surface trough across the local area. The combination of diurnal instability and convergence along the trough axis produced a few strong to severe storms across inland areas.
episodes.170564: Showers and thunderstorms developed over areas with large dew point depressions. The result was isolated strong, brief outflow wind gusts.
episodes.170596: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northwestern Nebraska during the mid afternoon hours of June 29th. As this activity tracked east into the northwestern Sandhills and portions of North Central Nebraska, it intensified, leading to thunderstorm wind gusts of around 60 MPH. A 63 MPH wind gust was reported at the Valentine Airport.
episodes.171203: A weak cold front drifted into the region while a series of upper disturbances moved across the region. This produced multiple rounds of mainly afternoon storms, some of which became severe.
episodes.171359: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Iowa during the early evening of June 28th. These storms dropped some hail with the largest reported being half dollar sized near Kendallville (Winneshiek County).
episodes.171380: A cluster of slow moving thunderstorms produced some isolated flash flooding across southern portions of Dale county.
episodes.171425: Thunderstorms produce hail in and around the Prescott area. Most reports were 1/2 to 3/4 inches in diameter.  One inch diameter hail fell in Prescott. Severe thunderstorms winds were reported near Kirkland as well.
episodes.171530: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were scattered reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
episodes.171537: A cluster of slow moving thunderstorms developed in the Valdosta area with rainfall amounts between 3 and 6 inches falling in a short period of time. This resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.171559: Thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona. Thunderstorm winds produced a wall of dust and downed power lines northwest of Tucson while heavy rain caused flash flooding in the Baboquivari Mountains.
episodes.171645: A cluster of showers and storms tracked across northern Michigan during the afternoon and evening of 6/28, eventually moving out over Lake Huron. These storms produced wind gusts near 50 mph over the nearshore waters of Lake Huron.
episodes.171742: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.171841: An increase of monsoonal moisture resulted in multiple storms with microburst wind gusts in northern Utah, as well as flash flooding in portions of southern Utah.
episodes.171875: Another active afternoon and evening of summertime convection produced reports of scattered wind damage, quarter size hail, and  0.50 to 2.0 inches over portions of north and central Georgia, with the highest amounts observed over the west Atlanta metro. These amounts of 1.5 to 5 inches occurred in Carroll and Douglas county, and were enough to cause flash flooding in the latter.
episodes.172093: A cold front trying to move through the region began to stall as it reached south Louisiana. This boundary became the focus for numerous showers and thunderstorms. One of those storms over New Orleans metro was producing frequent lightning. A roofer was struck and killed by a lightning strike in Metairie.
